rv.q: But in 2009, Anthony Page’s smart, engaging production for the Roundabout Theater Company makes it clear that this greatest of 20th-century plays is also entertainment of a high order.
This production restores the deep melancholy that can be lost when the play is performed as a vaudeville turn, and it finds the terror within the comedy.
And it's "9 to 5" that gets the last laugh.
"The principal asset in "9 to 5: The Musical" is unquestionably the beloved screen property on which this eager-to-please adaptation is based.
You kinda want '9 to 5: The Musical' to be better than it is.
The show is wholly harmless and will have its fans, especially among its target demographic.
From start to finish, it does what it's supposed to do -- and no more.

The awkward but lovely moments in which Reeves and Winter’s decades-long friendship is evoked — an urgent embrace, a coat draped over a sleeping body, a gentle caress, clasped hands — are among the most touching representations here
'9 to 5' is a female-empowerment theme-park musical - complete with a spunky Dolly Parton impersonator and lots of faceless scenery.

"In the current Roundabout Theatre Company production at Studio 54-the former disco is an ironic location for this desolate comedy-drama-director Anthony Page and his brilliant cast neatly sidestep that pitfall and dance a merry gig around it.
The ones in this presentation work very well for me.
It's simple, gorgeous, effective and relentlessly watchable.
Folks yearning for an old-fashioned musical may finally get their wish as the 1980 movie "9 to 5" arrives on Broadway.
9 to 5 aims low and hits its target squarely.

Is "9 to 5" as hip as TV's "The Office" or as joyously hit-filled as "How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying"? No, but if you're looking for a little diversion, it will do the trick from 8 to 10:15.

"9 to 5" had the potential to be a great musical comedy. And while faint hints of a crowd-pleaser occasionally occur, sitting through this faithful adaptation feels as tiresome as a long day at the office.
